result.note: Tests the terms of the February 2026 US-India interim trade framework: tariff commitments, the non-binding purchase pledge and the Section 232 condition on pharmaceuticals.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the US-India joint statement on a framework for an Interim Trade Agreement, released in February 2026:
items: The United States applies a reciprocal 18% tariff on Indian goods, with its removal conditional on the interim pact being concluded.
India takes on a binding obligation to purchase USD 500 billion of US goods over five years.
India commits to eliminating or reducing tariffs on all US industrial goods.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong. The USD 500 billion purchase over five years, covering energy, aircraft, GPUs and coking coal, is a signal of intent, not an obligation. The framework is a bridge to the broader Bilateral Trade Agreement talks launched in February 2025.
questions.source: India signals intent, not obligation, to purchase USD 500 billion of US goods over five years

questions.prompt: Under the US-India framework for an Interim Trade Agreement announced in February 2026, US tariff relief for Indian pharmaceuticals was deferred until the conclusion of which of the following?
options: A Section 301 unfair trade practices investigation
A World Trade Organization dispute panel ruling
questions.explain: The United States deferred pharmaceutical relief until a Section 232 national security investigation concludes. It did agree to lift steel, aluminium and copper tariffs on Indian aircraft and parts and to grant India a preferential tariff-rate quota for auto parts.
questions.source: defer pharmaceutical relief until a Section 232 national security investigation concludes.
